title: AI-assisted X-rays flag 18,377 people for TB testing in Delhi slums, 877 confirmed: Study
key_facts: PTI's report of 6 Oct 2026 covers a study published on 23 Aug 2026 in the Indian Journal of Tuberculosis.
An AI tool (Qure.ai) analysed digital chest X-rays from 168,568 residents in urban slums of Delhi; 18,377 (10.9%) were flagged for TB testing.
Of those flagged, 16,866 (91.7%) completed molecular testing, and 877 were confirmed with TB (5.2% of those tested).
The programme covered 349 notified urban slum clusters in six districts; it ran from July 2025 and was evaluated in April 2026.
The researchers say symptom-based screening misses people: more than 40 per cent of bacteriologically confirmed TB cases in a national survey did not report usual symptoms.
The AI did not give the final diagnosis; sputum samples were sent for molecular testing.
quote_evidence: The AI did not provide the final diagnosis; people whose X-rays were flagged were offered sputum collection, with samples sent through programme networks for molecular testing to confirm TB.
The researchers said the tool could address a key limitation of symptom-based TB screening, since many TB cases may not present with the symptoms commonly used to identify people for testing.
why_it_matters_hint: AI-assisted screening could find TB cases that symptom checks miss, but most flagged people were not confirmed with TB.
